These pages are the **lab part** of the course *Big Data and Data
Analysis* (02053116) of the Faculty of Business. Every Sunday there is
one lab of 60 minutes on the lab computers. The lab part covers two
outcomes of the course, one after the other:

- **Labs 1–3 · C1, a big data platform.** You use **Google BigQuery**, a
  cloud platform that keeps tables of hundreds of millions of rows: you
  find data, load your own data, process it with SQL and show it on a
  dashboard in Looker Studio.
- **Labs 4–8 · C3, a real big data problem in R.** You solve one problem
  of a real online shop, step by step, in **R** and **RStudio**: read the
  data, clean it, explore it with charts, build a simple model and report
  the answer.

**How a lab works.** About 15 minutes on the interactive page of the lab:
the teacher shows each idea on a simulator. Then you follow the
**worksheet** (PDF) alone on the lab computer, step by step: every step
shows its screen. At home, the simulators of the page work on a phone, and
the video of the lab on the e-learning platform shows every step again.

**What you need.** A lab computer (Windows) with the Internet. Labs 1–3: a
personal **Google account** (Gmail); always **sign out** at the end of the
lab. Labs 4–8: R and RStudio, installed on the lab computers (free, also
for your own computer).

**Textbook.** Marz, N. and Warren, J. *Big Data: Principles and Best
Practices of Scalable Real-Time Data Systems*, Manning, 2015.
